rules.title: Authorized list
rules.text: In service writing, abbreviations used are those shown in Section 16 of this manual.

rules.title: Other abbreviations/acronyms
rules.text: Other abbreviations/acronyms may be used if the writer considers them helpful; they must be explained the first time they appear in the text (e.g. 'Covering Forces (CF)') or listed in a separate annex, unless they are already in Section 16, in general use (e.g. UN, NATO), or specialist abbreviations well understood by writer and recipients.

rules.title: Consistency throughout a document
rules.text: Once a word has been abbreviated, it is to be abbreviated throughout the same document.

rules.title: Composite Nouns/Verbs
rules.text: A composite noun or verb, or one containing a prefix or suffix, may be abbreviated by abbreviating the part for which there is an authorized abbreviation, e.g. mob (mobilize), demob (demobilize), minefd (minefield). Exceptions apply where there is an authorized abbreviation that itself carries the prefix/suffix, e.g. C attk (counter attack).

rules.title: Full Stops and Commas
rules.text: Full stops are not used in abbreviations or between a person's initials or decorations/qualifications. Commas are used after the name and between abbreviations of branches, decorations, qualifications, and service/regiment/corps.

rules.title: Plurals
rules.text: Some abbreviations serve for both singular and plural and do not take 's'. Abbreviations of measurements remain unaltered in the plural (e.g. m, l, hr). Where 's' is needed it is placed at the end of the abbreviation (e.g. GOCs) and only applies to noun abbreviations.

rules.title: Verbs
rules.text: An authorized present-indefinite abbreviation for a verb is used for all derivatives and tenses of that verb (e.g. sp for support, supported, supporting). Exceptions apply to abbreviations for a specific tense/derivative only, e.g. bldg (building), retd (retired), addl (additional).

rules.title: Multiple Meanings
rules.text: Some abbreviations serve two or more meanings (see Annex B to Section 16), e.g. AB for 'air borne' and 'after burner'. In case of possible confusion the word should be written in full.

rules.title: Ampersand
rules.text: An ampersand '&' is used instead of 'and' where appropriate in departmental and similar titles, e.g. AA&QMG, R&D.

rules.title: Compass Points
rules.text: The four cardinal points of the compass are always written in full in small letters (e.g. north). Intermediate points may be abbreviated using initial letters (NE, NNE) or written in full with a hyphen (north-east).

rules.title: Capitals
rules.text: If the first letter of an abbreviated item is shown in capitals in Section 16, it is written in capitals throughout its use anywhere.

rules.title: When abbreviations may/should not be used
rules.text: Maximum use of abbreviations is made in operational and non-operational writing and signal messages, EXCEPT: paragraph headings of operational and administrative orders; and, in non-operational writing, demi-official, commanded, and formal letters and service papers (except for decorations, qualifications, and Arms/Services). BAF may use abbreviations in service papers on operational matters.

rules.title: Allied Forces and Non-service Authorities
rules.text: No Section 16 abbreviations are used when corresponding with allied forces and non-service authorities. Officially recognized general abbreviations (e.g. WASA, PDB) may be used except in correspondence with foreign organizations. Operational writing addressed to para-military forces may use abbreviations.

rules.title: Multiple meanings (Section 16 introduction)
rules.text: Where an abbreviation has two or more approved meanings, alternative meanings are listed alphabetically at Annex B to Section 16. The author must ensure the intended meaning is clear from context.

rules.title: Signal messages use a separate list
rules.text: Signal messages use special abbreviations and rules in addition to the general list (see Section 15), e.g. CLN, QUES, PAREN — these have been excluded from the general abbreviations at Annex A to Section 16.

rules.title: Rank/appointment prefix letters
rules.text: Where appropriate, the following letters may be added to authorize abbreviated titles: 'A' for assistant/acting (e.g. AMS = Assistant Military Secretary, A/MS = Acting Military Secretary); 'D' for deputy (e.g. DPM = Deputy Provost Marshal; 'Dy' may be used to avoid confusion, e.g. Dy MS); 'DA' for deputy assistant (e.g. DADOS); 'Offg' for officiating (e.g. Offg CO); 'V' for Vice (e.g. AVM, V Adm).

rules.title: Standard English abbreviations
rules.text: Widely used standard English abbreviations are also used in service writing where convenient, e.g. etc., e.g., i.e., pm, am, RSVP, viz, Mr., Mrs., BA, BSc, SOS.

rules.title: Military Qualifications
rules.text: Certain lower-case letter groups denoting military qualifications (afwc, awc, ndc, ndu, rcds, psc, te, etc.) are used only when they refer to the qualification itself, not to the institution.

rules.title: Date abbreviation
rules.text: A date is written day, month, year (e.g. 01 August 2022). Abbreviated: two-figure day, first three letters of the month, and optionally the last two digits of the year, e.g. 01 Aug 22.

rules.title: Formations, Units and Detachments
rules.text: Identifying numbers are written in Arabic numerals before the description (e.g. 11 Inf Div). Quantitative numbers of formations/units/ships/bases are always written in full (e.g. 'One division'). A formation/unit less a detached portion is described as e.g. '2 Inf Bde less two bns'.

rules.title: Abbreviations not normally used in certain letters
rules.text: Abbreviations are not normally used in commanded, formal, and demi-official letters (except for decorations, qualifications and Arms/Services). Service terminology and abbreviations should not be used in correspondence with civilian authorities or the public.
